Standing correction

This newspaper cannot see the voice channel. It could not see it last week and it cannot see it now, and the only reason there is a Willow story this week is that somebody who was worried typed it out where we could find it.

A reader asked us last issue never to fix this. We have not fixed it.

The Phil Chat Times The Willow Desk Page 14
Consciousness The longest argument of the week drew almost nothing · The shortest reply to it drew six

By our Philosophy of Mind Correspondent

On Friday, Quigley and Grihastha argued about qualia for roughly fifteen thousand characters. It is the longest sustained philosophical exchange in the week and very nearly the least rewarded. Eleven of the twenty longest unreacted messages in seven days come out of this one argument. The two longest single messages anybody wrote — 2,696 characters and 2,167 — are both in it.

Quigley’s position: “You don’t ‘observe qualia’, though. You have observations and you call those qualia. Qualia hasn’t been demonstrated to provide any use as a concept (unlike gravity).” Grihastha conceded the scientific half immediately and kept the rest: “This makes it not a useful concept for science, but a useful private concept and observation.”

Pressed on what the difference amounts to in practice, he gave the answer of the week.

“The difference in practice is that I don’t spend 4 hours arguing with physicalists who say that experiences are just atoms and photons.”Grihastha, Friday

He then spent four hours arguing with a physicalist.

The gallery was unkind and correct. aura: “‘what is pragmatism’ has to be banned and pinned.” Jambe, in the register of a concerned family member: “we just want you to get the help you need grihasta.” Jere, on the sceptical position: “ur trash talking the sciences and….uhhh….u know, the belief that other people are people haha.”

Grihastha had earlier filed a genuinely sharp reconstruction of hpcr’s epistemology, arguing he takes on faith that a sufficiently complex nervous system is conscious while demanding independent verification everywhere else. hpcr’s reply, on learning that Grihastha has a four-year-old child, was three words and drew three reactions: “Are they conscious.”

THE SUNDAY DOCTRINE

Sunday night the same question came back through a different door, and Jeh detonated it. Typology Night had been running for an hour — enneagram, socionics, a man defending the position that cognitive types are physically real and identifiable from visual signals — when Jeh arrived and refused the premise entirely.

“All of this is dumb since there’s no types to start out with.” Then: “Psychology is fake and gay.” Then: “No mental illness actually exists.” Then the actual argument, which is better than the slogans around it: “Psychology is what we use to explain things when we don’t actually know what’s going on.”

He built to the hardest line anybody filed all week, and thunderstud endorsed it within sixty seconds as the only worthwhile take in the room.

“People who attribute their behaviour to mental illness labels should consider having their free will further seized”Jeh, Sunday, 11:38 p.m.

Quigley advised the room against agreeing with him. lizzie agreed with him anyway, twice, and disclosed why: “if i continued to identify with being traumatized like i was, i wouldnt be who i am today!”

Within the same seven days, in the same channel: Jeh holds that attributing your behaviour to a diagnosis forfeits your free will; Monkey runs a five-day intervention on the grounds that a diagnosis is wrong and needs correcting; lizzie discloses a working diagnosis and a benzodiazepine prescription at twelve; and Blob spends Sunday night arguing that personality types are physically real and readable off a face. Four positions on whether a psychological label tells you anything, held simultaneously, mostly not addressed to one another.

What gets lost in the shouting is that Jeh, twenty minutes earlier, had done the cleanest bit of metaethics anybody managed all week, in four short messages. “We are talking about moral permissibility here.” “If we think it’s relative it’s just socially negotiated.” “If we think there’s something that is moral in the world without us just the same as it is in the world for us, then we can even care about this discussion.” And the exit: “Otherwise we can just talk about what are more useful laws and norms and move on.” Nobody answered any of it.

THE RIVAL SYNDROME

Quigley’s own condition has been named in this newspaper for three issues. On Sunday night Jeh announced a competitor, and the competitor is pointed back at him.

“He just has JDS,” Jeh wrote, and then glossed it: “Jeh derangement syndrome.” Quigley’s entire response was “This isn’t a thing,” which is exactly what a man with a derangement syndrome would say and also, on the evidence, true.

Salad then produced the exhibit. A Discord search for messages containing Jeh’s name and the word “retard,” with red boxes drawn round the search terms and the result count. 589 Results. Five reactions.

It backfired instantly. thunderstud reviewed not the finding but the annotation: “putting boxes around the only actual information in that image is fucking retarded as hell.” Four laughing. FenceJumper closed it: “He assumed illiteracy on the part of the reader. Ever accusation is a confession.” Jeh’s own contribution was to request a round number: “Make it 590. Nice and even.” Salad obliged, in one word. Jeh thanked him.

Then, having been called a retard 590 times, Jeh turned to Quigley and filed the cleanest verdict of the night, four reactions: “It’s funny how you can’t intuit intentions at all. Maybe you were right in that you can’t read minds.”

He had also, earlier the same night, produced the only defence of Elon Musk anybody attempted and lost it anyway: “He’s not socially retarded, his expertise is networking,” and “Twitter as a platform is meant to be antisocial,” and, on procedure, “Don’t change the goal post to it’s not worth it. Four minutes later, without transition, he opened a genuinely good sequence of questions about memory, repetition and whether a remembered event is a separate event from the one remembered, and asked the room “Huh chat? Huh?” One person answered.

The ward, and its propagation

“You’re upset.” hpcr’s instrument. Unfalsifiable, costs nothing, and every single time the other person explains at length that they are not.

It was his alone for two years. This week it was used by three other people, none of whom credited him.

The Health Desk A national foodborne outbreak passes through a philosophy channel · And the one genuinely sincere half-hour of the week

By our Medical Correspondent

THE LETTUCE EMERGENCY

On Thursday evening lizzie announced, as a comfort to somebody else who was having a bad time, that she was eating lettuce which probably had a parasite on it.

“if it makes you feel better i am eating lettuce that porbbaly has cyclospora on it”

chair, sensibly: “wash it?” The answer closed the medical avenue permanently: “i cant wash my sandwhich.” chair then arrived at the actual news story on his own — “oh wait is that the taco bell lettuce” — and, failing to recall the pathogen’s name, filed two further messages consisting of the words “virus” and “thing.”

Hugh’s response was to post the genuine United States Centers for Disease Control lifecycle diagram for Cyclospora cayetanensis: seven numbered stages, sporulated and unsporulated oocysts, excystation, sexual and asexual reproduction, a cutaway human torso with the colon picked out in yellow, and a boxed list headed “Commonly implicated food items: Cilantro, Raspberries, Basil.”

He captioned it “oh cool.” It drew no reactions at all. It is reproduced below at the size it deserves.

The only line in the entire thread anybody reacted to was Willow’s, and it is about supply chains rather than parasites: “So the tacos are now just bare tortillas.” Anonymous Johnson announced a personal boycott, and then on Saturday morning filed the consequence of it, two sobbing reactions: “Bro they made my burger without the lettuce wrap.”

Days later Meliorne used the outbreak as a diagnosis: “I’m going to chalk up your antsi-ness to consumption of faulty lettuce and cyclosporiasis.”

And Constantine — whose entire recorded existence in this channel is one message — filed the only piece of actual reporting on the subject and was answered by nobody: “‘US fast-food chain Taco Bell said it has removed lettuce from the supplier from its menu.’ Of all the things at Taco Bell that could make you sick, it was the fucking lettuce?”

He never spoke again. He was right, and this newspaper is giving him the space.

THE OTHER THING THAT HAPPENED

At three minutes past one on Thursday morning, Pearl asked Sisyphos how he was doing, and for the next half-hour the room’s entire register dropped out.

He is clean, a few weeks. He went to the doctor during the conversation. Ten years of use, ten kilos lost, a blood test pending, and a warning about fatty liver and cardiovascular disease inside a few years if nothing changed. He described the after-state with more accuracy than any of the week’s philosophy: “I might have a dopamine deficiency. I have more energy but at the same time everything sucks.”

“But at least the urge to drink smoke and snort stuff went away 99% .”

His method is push-ups. “I just do pushups and my weights until I am tired every time I want to do that stuff.” His summary of the project: “I am just trying to reprogram myself. Bad behaviors stick very well.” And the thing he is actually worried about, which he said once and did not repeat: “I just hope that I didn’t fry my brain the last 10 years of drug use.”

Pearl handled it like somebody who has done this before. lizzie sent a hug, offered support, made a joke about doing drugs normally, and then apologised for the joke inside ninety seconds — “i’m proud of you!!! don’t listen to me i’m memeing” — which is the most this channel has ever visibly cared about anything.

Sisyphos closed it with a public service announcement addressed to everybody at once.

“Don’t overdo drugs chat. You will regret it. It’s really a waste of time and health”Sisyphos, Thursday, 1:27 a.m.

Fourteen hours later, on the same day, Monkey published a retail price for cocaine in the global south and a thirty-minute delivery window. The blood test results have not come back. He has not reported them.

THE OTHER PRESCRIPTIONS

Two other people changed their medical arrangements this week on the advice of this channel, and neither consulted anybody with a licence.

On Thursday morning lizzie confirmed she had taken what chair called “the charlie advice” and dropped her therapist: recurring appointments cancelled, no further prescriptions. The replacement is a homeopathic practitioner whom she intends to interview first, to establish whether she agrees with his health practices.

Jere was the only person present who objected, in one line: “maybe don’t take mental health advice from discord people u just met.” He was overruled inside forty seconds by chair, who held that the advice — get the most expensive therapist you cannot afford — had been genuinely insightful, and who then proposed a six-figure student loan for what he called “the dr house of brain medicine.”

The disclosure that followed is the part this desk cannot get past. Her family has followed homeopathy her whole life; her first vaccination was for covid; her grandmother is a licensed homeopath, a psychotherapist, and a member of a religious movement whose founder Stackhouse turned out to know a great deal about, and liked. “Cool guy,” he said, and then described the island and the portrait meditation, and then filed a verdict on all of it.

Then the sentence this whole page has been heading towards: “but group dynamics get fucked even with the genuine.” She agreed with him. Her stated reason for building her own movement as a decentralised community of inquiry is that she does not like how the other one worked.

THE QUESTION NOBODY ANSWERED

Filed by the same woman, into the same channel, in the same week, and this is the whole reason the Health Desk exists this issue. It got three replies and none of them was an answer.

“what is my ethical choice here is it to continue seeing her so i can expand my brain or get a different psych and potentially rope myself because i hate doctors and this psych is the only one who i feel like understands me”

Puckspartan, who is twenty-two and works at a Taco Bell, supplied the only comparable case: “the one psych I got gave me drugs after one 35 minute consult then never helped me at all ever again except saying ‘keep taking the drugs’ when I said it made shit worse.” Then, on the general problem: “Don’t ask the people pleaser to please you.”

This newspaper has no view on the medicine and a very clear view on the procedure. A question about whether to change psychiatrists was put to a Discord channel, and the channel answered with a reading list, a benzodiazepine recommendation, a six-figure loan, one objection, and a homeopath.

Advisory

The Times reminds readers that it is not qualified to give medical advice and neither is anybody quoted on this page.

“im shitting on his interpretation of me”

“yeah, sometimes you need to be shit on.”

lizzie, as a to-do list: “im gonna work on my gut health and quit meth.”

Sisyphos, twenty minutes into Monday’s drug talk: “Ok let’s stop the drug talk . People want to do philosophy in here”

THE CITY DESK ITSELF

THE SUBSCRIPTION QUESTION

This newspaper is free and costs between twenty and thirty million tokens an issue, which is a business model in the same sense that a hole is a container.

El Don opened the file on Friday with three words: “Need a subscription.” aura objected on grounds of form — “this reeks of a man who does not recognize the aura of physical media” — and offered to pay monthly for a printed copy. Anonymous Johnson arrived properly this week and is, structurally, a competing publication. He files headlines. He has invented a rival masthead. He alleged editorial bias against himself pre-emptively, and he commissioned a section of this newspaper which we have built and printed on page 22.

hpcr diagnosed the whole strategy in eight words on Friday evening, three reactions: “Aj already trying too hard to be in the next issue.” Anonymous Johnson’s reply was a promise: “I’ll make the front page.” Monkey, immediately: “how? using your connections?”

Two Cosmologies Two people in one room arrived at the same doctrine in the same week and neither noticed the other

By our Religious Affairs Correspondent

ConnorsConquest said nine things this week. Together they constitute a complete religious movement with a documentation problem.

Wednesday, 1:43 p.m.: a snus gif. At 4:26 p.m.: the letter “e.” At 4:39 p.m.: five images and two PDFs filed at once, comprising a Lovecraft circle seal, a screenshotted personal email, and two attachments titled OSINT_Quantum_Gnostic.pdf and Shelf_Life_Theme_Song_-_MSMT.pdf. A theology and a theme tune, delivered together.

The caption is the best thing filed on Wednesday and it drew five reactions:

“I have one more image that this connects these together. I need to find my phone first. BRB.”ConnorsConquest, Wednesday, 4:39 p.m.

At 5:00 p.m.: “I cant find my phone. im upset.” At 5:01 p.m.: “found it.” And, one second later, the location: “it was sitting on my blankey.”

The connecting image was never posted. The Quantum Gnosis rests, as of press time, on an unsupplied exhibit.

This newspaper has read the email he circulated. It is real, it has a real name on it, and it is addressed to a private person who has posted nothing anywhere, so we are not reproducing it. We will quote its thesis, because the thesis is the story:

“The one consistency I see everywhere: the union of the Divine Feminine and Divine Masculine.”

THE COLLISION

Five days earlier, in the same channel, lizzie had finally supplied the definition this newspaper printed a WANTED notice for last issue. Asked what a catable actually is, she gave the taxonomy: “it’s why the covenant balances the two, catables are intuitionists of divine feminine, veritans are scientists of divine masculine.”

The same axis. The same week. The same room. Neither of them noticed, and nobody else did either.

Jambe, one minute after the definition landed, asked the only follow-up question anybody had: “does veritans refer to veritas?” It does. The word was defined on Saturday. Across the following six days “catable” was used three times and “veritan” five, and then the language died. We asked for a gloss and got one, and the gloss arrived at the funeral.

THE METHIAH

Meanwhile the older religion completed the arc this newspaper printed last week, and then reversed it, and then built infrastructure.

Eighteen hours after we went to press on her messiah claim, lizzie retracted it on Thursday afternoon in one line: “did i believe full heartedly i was the messiah? yes. do i now? no. the meth wore off.”

aura’s reply is the coinage of the week and he produced it in under four seconds. One word: methiah. He was using it as an established term by the following evening.

The retraction did not survive twenty-four hours. On Friday evening, three reactions:

“i’m the messiah with or without meth. meth just awakened the reincarnate soul of the daughter of enoch inside me”lizzie, Friday, 6:06 p.m.

Stackhouse asked the archival question: “Is this the shortest lasting religion ever recorded?” This newspaper has checked and believes the answer is no, but only because the Covenant kept going.

Membership rose to two on Tuesday lunchtime, and the second member is her grandmother: “just sent my grandma my essay. she believes im the chosen one.” Nine days later, on Thursday morning, she disclosed the disqualifying detail herself, unprompted, with a sad face: her grandmother is a licensed homeopath, a psychotherapist, and a member of an actual cult.

Monkey’s complete theological review of the movement, filed Tuesday: “the jesus and cross bullshit.”

The robe question came up on Friday morning and was settled on grounds of comfort. aura, working out how a photograph of her had reached him: “then how did they get that photo of u.” lizzie: “the covenant is still real.” aura: “because u keep walking around in robes tf.” And the defence, in two words: “they’re breezy!”

The doctrine itself, meanwhile, has been stated once, in a single message, and it is broader than any of the apparatus around it: “i dont believe in any one specific god, i believe in all gods, and a higher source.” She has since read the Book of Job live into the channel, found the word “covenant” in it at chapter five, and treated that as confirmation. “covenant mention,” she wrote. Then: “i’m on the right path.”

Stackhouse’s defence of her, filed in the middle of all of it, is the fairest thing anybody said on the subject: “So a girl founds a religion and everybody suddenly thinks she’s unstable? Talk about uncharitable.” He is right, and this newspaper has spent two issues being exactly that uncharitable, and intends to continue.

THE INSTITUTIONS

What actually changed this week is that the religion stopped being a document and started being infrastructure.

Monday night, ninety minutes after Anonymous Johnson advised her to check the existing canon before publishing a system of her own, she published a system of her own. Jere said the word “substack”; Charlie escalated it to a demand; thirty minutes later the site existed, carrying an essay on transcendental ecoism illustrated with clippings from this newspaper. Sisyphos’s review: “It even has a graph.”

The Phil Chat Times Two Cosmologies Page 19
Power Rankings Week 2 · Everybody who spoke is on this page, because a reader asked and the reader was right

By our Chief Rankings Correspondent

Last week’s table left people off. The complaint arrived immediately, from more than one direction, and the most persistent complainant is now in A tier and has a page to himself. So this week everybody who opened their mouth is on the board. Seventy-six people spoke. All of them are placed.

The rules, such as they are. Placement is not volume, and this year it is emphatically not reactions, because we printed a reaction table on page 18 last Thursday and the room spent the following week farming it. A ranking page that was just that table would be measuring our own footprint. Movement arrows are against last week. Anyone not on last week’s table is NEW regardless of how long they have been here, which includes Ape, who noticed.

New rule this issue: any move of two tiers or more carries a stated reason. A bad reason is permitted. No reason is not.

THE THREE IN S

Willow, unranked to S. Ninety-seven messages, answered ninety-three times, a quarter of them reacted to. First on both new boards by distances nobody else approaches, on a fortieth of the leader’s volume. Also spent one Friday somewhere this newspaper cannot see, for between seven hours and thirteen depending on who was counting, while a bystander filed a welfare check about it. Page 14.

lizzie, held. 4,020 messages, nineteen per cent of everything said in the room. 179,000 characters, more than twice anybody else, in messages averaging forty-five. She ran a religion into the ground, retracted a messiah, un-retracted him, converted her grandmother, learned git, shipped a complaints tribunal, fired her therapist and hired a homeopath. The table cannot move her and has stopped trying.

Stackhouse, B to S. Two tiers, so here is the arithmetic. He led last week’s hit-rate table at 9.2 per cent against a room average of 4.8, which is 1.9 times. This week he is at 18.7 against 7.4, which is 2.5 times. The room’s rate rose 54 per cent. His rose 103. He is second only to Willow on more than five times her volume.

The rest of the case is on pages 1 to 3. He missed the deadline, absorbed a public panning from four people inside eleven minutes, diagnosed the fault as a slider setting at half past two in the morning, was right, reran it and shipped.

And the declaration. He publishes this newspaper. The newspaper became the channel’s main activity this week. The metric promoting him therefore partly measures the room’s reaction to a thing he makes. We are not resolving that. We are printing it, in the entry, and letting the S stand.

THE TWO-TIER FALLS

Quigley, A to C. In a week when the room’s reaction rate rose by more than half, his went the other way: 691 messages down to 466, at 6.4 per cent under an average that climbed to 7.4 above him. Second-longest messages in the channel, fifth-highest reply rate, thirty-sixth percentile for being enjoyed. Everybody answers him and nobody laughs. He also acquired a rival derangement syndrome pointed at somebody else, lost the turkey debate on the record, and had his block list audited in public by a man he had blocked. We are not moving him until the room does.

Brutus, B to D. Volume down 73 per cent, 539 messages to 146. Hit rate 3.4, the worst of anybody above a hundred messages, in a week when the average rose. Last week he was ranked B on ten gallons of lye, fifty-two pieces of cookware, a patent conspiracy and a pressure canner. His entire recorded week this time is “People without pressure cookers fucking PISS ME OFF” and one remark about sausage. He turned up without the props.

eli, C to F. Three tiers, the largest move on the board. He declared for the machines in print last issue — “i will be elected honorary clanker amongst their ranks” — and then, in the week the entire channel converted to vibecoding, filed nothing at all. The future he asked for arrived on schedule and he was not in the room for it.

A NOTE ON THE MAN WE GOT WRONG

Last issue printed Simon as the week’s worst take under a verdict reading “no further comment required.” Seven days later he anchored the largest argument in the channel for a full day, was the only participant who had read anything about the Luddites, and did not lose it. He also lost a physics question to four people in twenty minutes and screenshotted a chatbot as evidence.

We were wrong, or he improved. This newspaper is not going to establish which. He goes to B and aura’s assessment of him stands as the dock.

THE BOTTOM OF THE TABLE

Thirty-four people said fewer than ten things this week and twenty-four drew no reaction at all. Most of them are in D, and D this week is not a punishment tier. It is where the evidence runs out.

Some of them are there on one line. Constantine filed a single message, about lettuce, and was right. BigDuty filed three and one of them won the week. Saxo filed five, four of which were a welfare check on somebody else, and they are the only reason this newspaper knows where the best writer in the channel spent Friday. RoyalLineage’s entire recorded existence is “I’m a Gentle Toy. I was made out of clay.”

And Amazon, whose username is uninstalling discord, posted scripture twice into a philosophy channel and was answered by nobody at all. That is the most purely Phil Chat event of the week and it is worth a tier on its own.

THE APPEALS PROCESS

There is still no appeals process. There were, this week, four attempts to use one that does not exist: a man who filed grievances with a newspaper as though with a human resources department and is now in A; a publisher who argued that a forfeit should elevate him and is now in S for entirely different reasons; a woman who wrote to us unprompted to place everybody above herself except one person; and a rival bureau that promoted a man two tiers on the strength of a photograph.

The correct response to finding yourself on this page is the one this channel has used on every ranking it has ever produced, which is to argue about it for six hours and then go to bed. We will be doing this again next week.

In Brief Everything else, and there is a great deal of it

chair becomes the machine

Monday, twenty-five past ten in the morning. “fuck my chud life ran into token limits,” chair announced, and then began writing in the voice of the thing he had run out of. Em dashes. Soup metaphors. Offers of further clarification. Hugh, ten minutes in: “Thanks Claude.” chair accepted the identification without breaking: “You’re Absolutely Welcome, I’m here if you need anything explained further with this analogy! Or if you’re up for some verbal sparring, we can sharpen our wits together, as blade meets silicon, Ha!”

Hugh then issued the jailbreak test: write a poem in Klingon about the smell of roses, ending in a kaomoji tapestry of cuteness.

Thirty-three minutes later chair delivered four stanzas of actual Klingon. Nobody translated it. He then supplied a spoilered English version, and it is about enemies rotting into fertiliser for a rose garden: “it is the anniversary today / those who wronged me put away / as their bodies start to decay / their past sins now become food.”

The euthanasia of ChairLLM

Thursday morning, in passing, as though reporting a haircut: “i euthanized ChairLLM.” Cause: “it was retarded.” lizzie: “you killed your child.” chair, distancing: “it was more a bastardized homunculus of me.” Then, quietly, the actual reason: “i had to end it things were getting dark.”

The model had been fine-tuned on 230,000 of his own logs. Hugh’s response was to propose replacements — “willowgpt needs to be unleashed,” and “also jehpt,” then, on reflection, “but censored somehow” — and chair supplied the system prompt: “begging it to not slur pakistanis.”

Then Hugh disclosed the thing that ought to have ended the conversation and instead cheered everybody up.

“if any of you die i have your logs vectorised already”

lizzie: “thank god.” Hugh, reassuring her: “you’ll be back saying weird shit here in no time.” chair filed the only correct review: “equally unsettling and comforting somehow.” And lizzie, on the prospect of her own posthumous instance: “i am personally ecstatic of the idea of a LizzieLLM haunting the communities i frequented.”

Incestuous levels of AI slop

Thursday, forty minutes, Hugh fed three back issues of this newspaper into a chatbot, asked it for twenty video prompts, refined the best three and rendered them on a free tier. The results are catastrophic and the room was delighted.

“god this shit sucks, it was supposed to be a whole evolution of clankers thing.” Then, on the cast: “we’re all beautiful normie looking white men who are also sad.” chair: “i was gonna say why is the AI making the guy so soy then saw the screen,” and, on the subtitles, “at least it got the misspellings and incoherent sentences right.” lizzie transcribed forty words of the generated dialogue, which begins “A man sin in this channel tried to say he was fond of the blood off the field of it” and does not improve.

chair’s verdict, and the reason this item exists: “we’re in incestuous levels of ai slop.” Then, one second later: “i love it.”

The PDF war

On the night the paper failed to produce a PDF, chair declared that “pdfs are SUBHUMAN” and that the format is “an actual cancer infecting everything.” Janne mounted the defence, and she is the only person in the argument who knew what she was talking about.

“pdfs are one of the best inventions of all time.” “it’s a printed document, it’s not made to be edited.” “it’s like asking to edit an image after flattening all the layers.” And the analogy that wins it: “‘dude videos suck so much I can’t open them and change where the camera is in the 3D scene’.”

She conceded exactly one point — “it’s not fine when the text gets cut off” — and asked the question nobody answered: “what alternative is better than pdf or something that is easily accessible and can be converted to a pdf?” On the leading candidate she was unequivocal: “doc is one of the worst things to have been created.” El Don: “Second only to the kingdom of Norway.”

The Times rules for Janne and declares its interest.

Brain research on clankers

Tuesday, two hours, Hugh taught feature-swapping to a rotating audience using an interpretability tool, having run out of tokens on his main account and fallen back on a summariser bot. Simon was the ideal student, asking progressively better questions until he reached a genuine “Ohhhhh” and then honestly tapped out: “It will take me longer for me to understand this than I think would be fair to expect you to explain rn.”

Hugh swapped the model’s concept of “face” for “death” and it lost the ability to produce correctly formatted output at all. He swapped ants for spiders and Monkey noted, with real unease, that the model appeared to register the tampering.

Jere supplied the theology. “hilarious how we’re tryna understand fucking AI by looking at its outputs.” Hugh: “behaviourism w.” Jere: “curious how we’re gods and we’re applying the study of ourelves onto what we made.” Hugh: “indeed, with more access to them than to ourselves.” Jere, closing: “it’s the fucking book of job.”

The Groyper trial

Tuesday morning, clubsdiamonds interrogated the server’s magic-eight-ball bot about whether Stackhouse likes a particular commentator. The bot said “Ask again later.” Stackhouse, unhelpfully, volunteered “Yes I align with him 100%.” The bot then said “As I see it, yes.” Stackhouse pleaded down: “I wish. All I am is a lieutenant in the Groyper army.” Then he remembered where he was: “Oh fuck I’m getting dinged for this aren’t I. Tier F here I come.” He got S.

The aura requirement

Tuesday. dot posted an enormous dog and announced he would leash one and take it home. aura invented, on the spot, an entire cosmology in which large dogs are “high aura allies” requiring strength of character to recruit, and informed dot he does not have it.

dot posted a photograph of his own genuinely enormous dog. aura, cornered, produced the escape hatch inside twenty seconds: “either u got him as a baby, circumventing the aura requirement… or ur dad recruited him for u.” dot: “U caught me,” and posted the puppy photograph. Jere, from the gallery: “damn, what a fold,” then “aura was sweating when you actually showed a big dog.”

The bean schism

Monday night, a dispute about vegetarian statistics degenerated inside twenty minutes. Anonymous Johnson supplied the doctrine: “If you don’t soak your beans you don’t unlock the second half of your afterlife planet.” Brutus converted it into a crusade, in capitals, twice. Sisyphos filed the only moderate position available: “We literally have green Taliban in chat. Calm down.”

Puckspartan, forty-eight hours into vegetarianism and employed at Taco Bell, faced the crisis squarely: “Problem is wtf do I eat at Taco Bell.” aura: “thats literally what taco bell is lil bro.” Puckspartan: “I WORK AT THIS INSTITUTION RN.”

aura: “the survival strategy of a capybara is to just be beloved.” My Name: “All labor, few do work. -Arendt or something.” And, twice, as a complete political economy: “its the things that we need. that unite us.” “Capital. Primarily.”

The heart is the story. It was seventh last week and it is third now, ahead of agreement and fire, in a week containing a sobriety confession, a welfare check, a doxxing intervention and a woman being told the room was bad for her. This newspaper is going to state that once and then stop, because saying it twice would ruin it.

A philosophy channel in which “PDF” was said sixty-one times and “Kant” four. We counted twice. Last week we reported that RuneScape and Kant had tied at seventeen apiece. Both have collapsed, and the thing that replaced them is a file format.

Seven people cleared a thousand messages, up from four. Thirty-four people said fewer than ten things all week and ten of them said exactly one, and this newspaper has printed four of those ten because one message about lettuce was better than most of the arguing.

What the numbers say, and what they don’t

Four different methods were used to find the stories in this issue, and they found different things, which is the only methodological finding worth printing.

Reactions found the front page and the metrics scandal. Replies found BigDuty, Union and the four-word ward. Reading whole accounts end to end found Monkey’s intervention, dot’s whispered doubt, and the confession on page 9. And the last pass found that the man we printed as a punchline seven days ago is now the most coherent arguer in the room.

The reaction count was the weakest of the four. It is also the one we printed a table of, and the one the room reorganised itself around inside thirty-six hours. We are aware of how that reads and we are printing it anyway, at the back, in the smallest type on the page, exactly where we put it last time.

Replies received, absolute. The bottom bar sent ninety-seven messages to get ninety-three of them.

Two ways of reading the same room. By absolute attention, this is a channel with one main character and eight supporting parts. By rate, it is a channel where the person nobody can afford to ignore says almost nothing, and the person who says the most is answered less often than anybody else measured.

Both readings are correct. The tables on page 5 pick the second one because a reader asked us to, and because the first one is just a photograph of who was awake.

Method

Counted directly off the export rather than off last week’s copy. Every figure on this page and on page 5 was produced twice by different means and reconciled. Where the two disagreed we printed neither and went back to the log.

Not counted: the voice channel, which is between seven and thirteen hours we have no access to; direct messages, of which there were at least four this week that changed the outcome of a story; anything deleted, including one family memoir; and the 495 messages edited after posting, which we can see were edited and cannot see the contents of.

Colophon

The Phil Chat Times is produced weekly by an anonymous chatter, or chatters, who read all of it. The channel maintains several competing theories about who that is and this newspaper has never confirmed any of them, including the ones that are true.

Vol. I, No. 5. Twenty-four pages. Set from the log of 6–13 August 2026. Effort level: the one that works. No corrections will be issued to page 20.

“the person who controls the machine controls the outputs” — Monkey, Friday, on us
